mainTopic: Who can make a תמורה: an heir, a woman, a minor, and a גוי, and whether the מקדיש or the מתכפר decides.
overview: The amud begins by finishing how רבי מאיר learns that an heir does סמיכה: the end stage of a holy animal is learned from its beginning stage. רבי יהודה, who holds an heir cannot make a תמורה, uses "ואם המר ימיר" to include a woman. רבי מאיר learns women from the extra ו in "ואם." The גמרא asks why any verse is needed for women, since "איש או אשה" already makes women equal to men for all punishments. It answers that תמורה is different, because the public and partners cannot make one. Next, רמי בר חמא asks whether a minor near adulthood can make a תמורה, and then whether a גוי can. רבא tries to answer the גוי question from a ברייתא that says a gentile's offerings have no תמורה. The גמרא then narrows the question to a גוי who consecrates for a ישראל, and begins to answer it from רבי יוחנן's rule that the מתכפר makes the תמורה. That rule continues on the next amud.

steps.title: An heir does סמיכה because the end of הקדש is learned from its beginning
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר compares the final stage of a קרבן (bringing it, with סמיכה) to its first stage (holiness and תמורה). Since an heir can make a תמורה, an heir can also do סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he learns the end stage of a holy animal from its beginning stage: just as at the beginning an heir can make a substitution, so too at the end an heir can lean his hands on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of רבי מאיר's source that an heir (יורש) does סמיכה on an animal he inherited.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר already knows an heir can make a תמורה, which belongs to the beginning stage of the animal's holiness. He uses that to learn the end stage, when the animal is brought and the owner does סמיכה. So the heir is treated like the original owner at both stages.

keyTerms.meaning: An heir, someone who inherited the holy animal from his father
The beginning stage of the animal's holiness
The end stage, when the animal is actually brought as a קרבן
Makes a substitution (תמורה)
Leans his hands on the animal's head before it is slaughtered (סמיכה)

phrases.english: And he derives the end of consecration from the beginning of consecration:
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי מאיר. The "end" means bringing the קרבן, which is when סמיכה happens.

phrases.english: just as at the beginning of consecration an heir can substitute,
so too at the end of consecration an heir leans his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion (before this section) of רבי מאיר's source for an heir doing סמיכה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns the end stage from the beginning stage: an heir can make a תמורה, so an heir can also do סמיכה.

steps.title: How does רבי יהודה use the extra words "ואם המר ימיר"?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that an heir cannot make a תמורה. So what does he learn from the doubled phrase that רבי מאיר used to include an heir?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יהודה, what does he do with this verse, "And if he shall at all substitute"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה learns from the doubled phrase "המר ימיר," since he does not use it to include an heir.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר learned from the extra wording that an heir can make a תמורה. רבי יהודה disagrees about heirs, but the doubled wording is still in the פסוק. The גמרא assumes no extra words are wasted, so they must teach רבי יהודה something else.

keyTerms.meaning: "He shall surely substitute", a doubled verb that seems extra and is used for a דרשה
"What does he do with it?", meaning what does he learn from this verse

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, this phrase "and if he shall at all substitute":
what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הַאי ״וְאִם הָמֵר יָמִיר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי מאיר's use of the verse to רבי יהודה's use of the same verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי יהודה learns from the doubled phrase "המר ימיר," since he does not use it to include an heir.

steps.title: The doubled phrase includes a woman, as a ברייתא teaches
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses "המר ימיר" to include a woman in the laws of תמורה. A ברייתא supports this: the whole section is written in the masculine, so a verse is needed to include women.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include a woman. As a ברייתא teaches: since the whole section speaks only in the masculine, as it says, "He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it," how do we know a woman is included? The verse says, "And if he shall at all substitute," to include a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה learns from the extra words that a woman can also make a תמורה. It then quotes a ברייתא that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section of תמורה uses only male language ("he shall not exchange it"). Without a special source, someone might think the law covers only men. The ברייתא says the doubled verb is that special source for women.

keyTerms.meaning: To include, meaning a verse adds a case that would not otherwise be covered
Male language, the verse is written as if speaking only about a man
"From where?", asking for a source
"The verse teaches", introducing the source that answers the question

phrases.english: To include a woman.
And as it is taught in a baraita: Since the entire matter
speaks only in the masculine,
as it is stated: "He shall not exchange it, nor substitute it,"
from where do we know a woman is included?
The verse states: "And if he shall at all substitute"
to include a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 and backs up the answer with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה uses "המר ימיר" to include a woman in תמורה, as the ברייתא says.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly derives women from "ואם המר ימיר."

steps.title: Where does רבי מאיר learn that a woman is included?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר already used "המר ימיר" for an heir. So what is his source for women?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי מאיר, from where does he learn that a woman is included?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns back to רבי מאיר: since he used the doubled verb for an heir, it asks where he learns that women are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each extra word can usually teach only one thing. רבי מאיר spent "המר ימיר" on the heir, so he needs a different source for women.

keyTerms.meaning: "From where does he know it?", asking a specific sage for his source

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Meir, from where does he derive a woman?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רבי יהודה's source for women is known, the גמרא asks for רבי מאיר's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רבי מאיר's source that a woman can make a תמורה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר learns women from the extra ו in "ואם"
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns women from the extra letter ו ("and") in "ואם." רבי יהודה does not learn anything from that ו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from "And if." And רבי יהודה does not expound "And if."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי מאיר learns women from the word "ואם," and explains that רבי יהודה does not make a דרשה from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have said just "אם" ("if"), but it says "ואם" ("and if"). רבי מאיר treats that extra ו as including women. רבי יהודה does not read meaning into that ו, so he needs the doubled verb for women. This explains why the two sages use the verse differently.

keyTerms.meaning: "He derives it", meaning this is where he learns the law from
"And if", the extra ו at the start is used for a דרשה
Expounds, learns a law from an extra word or letter

phrases.english: He derives it from "And if."
phrases.notes: The point is the extra ו, "and." The verse could have just said "if."

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda does not expound "And if."

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: "המר ימיר" includes an heir, and "ואם" includes a woman. רבי יהודה: an heir cannot make a תמורה, "המר ימיר" includes a woman, and "ואם" teaches nothing.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 4 and explains why רבי יהודה does not use the same source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns women from the extra ו of "ואם"; רבי יהודה does not expound "ואם."

steps.title: Inference: without a verse, a woman would not get lashes for תמורה
steps.stepSummary: Both sages need a verse to include women. That seems to imply that without the verse, a woman who made a תמורה would not get lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to both רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, the reason a woman is included is that a verse included her. This implies that if the verse had not included her, I would have said that when she makes a תמורה, she does not get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws an inference from both opinions to set up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sages search for a special verse to include women. That suggests that without it, women would be left out and would not receive lashes for doing תמורה. The next step will question this.

keyTerms.meaning: "The reason is...", introducing an inference about why a law applies
"I would have said", what we would think without this source
She gets lashes (מלקות)
Substitution, trying to switch a holy animal for another animal

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין רַבִּי מֵאִיר וּבֵין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: And according to both Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda,
the reason is that the verse included a woman,
but if the verse had not included her,

phrases.aramaic: הֲוָה אָמֵינָא: כִּי עָבְדָא תְּמוּרָה לָא לָקְיָא.
phrases.english: I would have said: when she performs substitution, she is not flogged.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵין רַבִּי מֵאִיר וּבֵין רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי קְרָא לְאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the shared point of both opinions (a verse is needed for women) and draws a surprising implication from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since both sages need a verse for women, it seems that without one, a woman who made a תמורה would not get lashes.

steps.title: But the Torah already treats women like men for all punishments
steps.stepSummary: רב, and also the school of רבי ישמעאל, teach from "איש או אשה" that a woman is like a man for every punishment in the Torah. So why would a special verse be needed for women in תמורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה say in the name of רב, and the school of רבי ישמעאל also taught: "When a man or woman shall commit any sin that people commit": the verse made a woman equal to a man for all punishments in the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the inference from step 6 by quoting a general rule that already makes women equal to men for all Torah punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a general verse already says women get every punishment men get, women would get lashes for תמורה with no special verse at all. So both רבי מאיר's "ואם" and רבי יהודה's "המר ימיר" seem unnecessary for women. The גמרא will need to explain why the תמורה verse is still needed.

keyTerms.meaning: "A man or a woman", the verse that puts both genders together
The verse made them equal
Punishments

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about whether women are included in תמורה. Everyone agrees they are. The question is only why a special verse is needed, since a general rule already seems to include them.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rav said,
and so too the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"When a man or woman shall commit
any sin that people commit":
the verse equated a woman with a man
for all punishments in the Torah!

steps.whyThisMatters: This general rule, that women and men are equal for Torah punishments, appears in many places in ש״ס. Here it forces the גמרא to explain what is special about תמורה.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, וְכֵן תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the inference drawn in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption, shared by רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה, that a special verse is needed to make a woman liable for lashes for תמורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general verse ("איש או אשה") already makes women equal to men for every Torah punishment, so the special verse for women in תמורה seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The special verse for women was still needed
steps.stepSummary: The general rule of 'איש או אשה' might only cover punishments that apply equally to everyone. תמורה does not apply to the public or to partners, so without a special verse we might have exempted women too.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. Otherwise you might say that the general rule only applies to a punishment that is the same for an individual and for the public. But here the punishment is not the same for everyone, as we learned: the public and partners do not make a תמורה. So you might think a woman also gets no lashes when she does it. The verse teaches us that she does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 7. It explains why the general rule from 'איש או אשה' was not enough for תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule says a woman is like a man for every punishment. But it might only cover punishments that apply to everyone, individual and public alike. תמורה already has exceptions (the צבור and שותפין are excluded), so we might have added women to the list of exceptions. The special verse blocks that mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary (the extra verse is not wasted)
Lest you say; introduces the mistaken idea the verse comes to prevent
An individual and the community
Partners who own something together
It teaches us (the point of the verse)

steps.whatToRemember: A broad rule may not reach a law that already has its own exceptions. That is why a specific verse can still be needed.

phrases.english: It was necessary, lest you say:
This applies only to a punishment
that is the same for an individual and for the public,
but here, since it is a punishment
that is not the same for everyone,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אֵין הַצִּבּוּר וְהַשּׁוּתָּפִין עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה
phrases.english: as we learned: the public and partners do not make a substitute

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה נָמֵי כִּי עָבְדָא לָא לָקְיָא,
phrases.english: a woman too, when she does it, would not get lashes,
so the verse teaches us that she does.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the public and partners are excluded from תמורה, a woman might be excluded too and get no lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The special verse teaches that a woman who makes a תמורה does get lashes.

steps.title: Can a minor make a substitution?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks whether a קטן can make a תמורה. The גמרא narrows the question to a minor who has reached the age of vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא asked: can a minor make a תמורה? What case is he asking about? If it is a minor who has not reached the age of vows, there is no question. He cannot even consecrate an animal, so he surely cannot make a תמורה. Rather, he is asking about a minor who has reached the age of vows.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רמי בר חמא asks about a minor, and the גמרא first pins down exactly which minor he means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A very young minor cannot consecrate at all, so he obviously cannot make a תמורה. The real question is about an older minor, near adulthood, whose vows already count. This step sets up the two sides of the question, which come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A minor, a child below the age of adulthood
That he make a תמורה, a substitute
What is the case? (asks for the exact situation)
The age at which a child's vows begin to count, just before adulthood
You should not ask; the answer is obvious

phrases.english: Rami bar Chama asked:
A minor, can he make a substitute?
What is the case?

phrases.aramaic: אִילֵּימָא בְּקָטָן שֶׁלֹּא הִגִּיעַ לְעוֹנַת נְדָרִים
phrases.english: If you say it is about a minor who has not reached the age of vows,
you should not ask,
because since he cannot even consecrate,
could he make a substitute?
Rather, when he asks,
it is about a minor who has reached the age of vows.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: קָטָן מַהוּ שֶׁיָּמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question after the topic of women is settled
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a minor who has reached the age of vows can make a תמורה

steps.title: The two sides of the minor question
steps.stepSummary: A minor near adulthood can consecrate, so maybe he can make a תמורה too. Or maybe not, because he cannot be punished, and תמורה carries a punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say: the Master taught that the verse says 'a man,' so why does it add 'when he clearly utters a vow'? To include a discerning minor close to manhood, whose consecration takes effect. Since he can consecrate, he can also make a תמורה. Or perhaps, since he is not subject to punishment, holiness does not take hold through his תמורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out both sides of רמי בר חמא's question about the minor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the verse 'כי יפליא נדר' shows that a מופלא סמוך לאיש can consecrate, and making a תמורה is a kind of consecrating. Side two: making a תמורה is forbidden and punished with lashes, and a minor cannot be punished. So maybe the Torah gave the power of תמורה only to someone who can be punished. The question is left open here.

keyTerms.meaning: A discerning minor close to adulthood, who understands what a vow means
His consecration is holy; it takes effect
Someone who can be punished
Takes hold (the holiness takes hold on the animal)
Or perhaps; introduces the other side of a question

steps.confusionAlert: Doing a תמורה is forbidden, yet it still works: the new animal becomes holy too. The question is whether the minor's act works at all, not whether he gets lashes.

phrases.english: Do we say, since the Master said:
"A man": why does the verse say "when he clearly utters a vow"?
To include a discerning minor close to manhood,
that his consecration takes effect.
Since he can consecrate,
he can also make a substitute.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו בַּר עוּנְשִׁין הוּא,
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since he is not subject to punishment,
holiness does not take hold through his substitution?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the two sides of the question defined in Step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the power to make a תמורה follow the power to consecrate, or the ability to be punished?

steps.title: If a minor can, what about a gentile?
steps.stepSummary: Even if a minor can make a תמורה because he will one day be subject to punishment, a גוי never will be. So can a גוי make a תמורה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if you say a minor can make a תמורה, because he will grow up and become subject to punishment, can a גוי make a תמורה? Maybe yes, since he can consecrate, as taught: why does the verse say 'איש איש'? To include gentiles, who can vow vow offerings and gift offerings like a Jew. So he can also make a תמורה. Or perhaps not: since he will never become subject to punishment, his תמורה is not holy.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא builds a second question on top of the first. Even if the minor can make a תמורה, a גוי is a harder case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a minor can make a תמורה, the reason may be that he will be punishable later in life. A גוי can consecrate offerings (from 'איש איש'), but he will never be subject to these punishments. So the second side of the question is stronger for a גוי than for a minor.

keyTerms.meaning: If you conclude; introduces a second question built on one answer to the first
He will come to be subject to punishments (when he grows up)
A non-Jew
Vow offerings and gift offerings

steps.whatToRemember: There is a ladder of cases. An adult woman makes a תמורה and gets lashes. A minor can consecrate and will be punishable later. A גוי can consecrate but will never be punishable. In steps 12–14, רבא tries to answer the question about a גוי from a ברייתא. Step 15 pushes that proof aside, and step 16 tries a new answer.

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר קָטָן עָבֵיד תְּמוּרָה,
phrases.english: If you say a minor can make a substitute,
because he will later become subject to punishments,
a gentile, can he make a substitute?
Do you say that since he can consecrate,
as it is taught: "Any man",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:18. The Hebrew literally says "a man, a man".

phrases.english: why does the verse say "a man, a man"?
To include gentiles,
who can vow vow offerings and gift offerings like a Jew,
so he can also make a substitute.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כֵּיוָן דְּלָא אָתֵי לִכְלַל עֳונָשִׁין,
phrases.english: Or perhaps, since he will never become subject to punishments,
when he makes a substitute, it is not holy?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם תִּימְצֵי לוֹמַר קָטָן עָבֵיד תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a further question on one possible answer to Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a גוי, who can consecrate but will never be punishable, can make a תמורה

steps.title: רבא brings a ברייתא about a gentile's offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a ברייתא, by רבי שמעון, that lists the rules of קדשי גוים. One of them is that they do not make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come and hear a ברייתא. Things a gentile consecrates: you may not benefit from them, but if you do, there is no מעילה. You are not liable for פיגול, נותר, or eating them while impure. A gentile cannot make a תמורה. Libations are not brought for them on their own, but his offering does need libations. This is רבי שמעון's view.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a ברייתא to answer the question from step 11 about whether a גוי can make a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists many ways a gentile's offering is treated more leniently than a Jew's. Inside the list is the line 'אין עושין תמורה', and that line is what רבא needs. The rest of the list is background.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals or items consecrated by gentiles
The sin of using consecrated property for yourself
An offering ruined by the wrong intention about when it will be eaten
Offering meat left over past its time limit
Wine (and flour-oil) offerings brought along with a sacrifice

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear, as it is taught in a ברייתא:
Things consecrated by gentiles:
one may not benefit from them, but one is not liable for misusing them,
and one is not liable for them because of פיגול,
נותר, or eating them while impure,
they cannot make a תמורה,
and libations are not brought for them on their own,
phrases.notes: A gentile doesn't bring libations as a separate offering, but his animal offering still comes with them.

phrases.english: but his offering requires libations,
these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question about a גוי from step 11.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a גוי can make a תמורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון listing the laws of קדשי גוים

steps.title: רבי יוסי is stricter
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says he would be strict on every item. The ברייתא also limits the 'no מעילה' rule to altar offerings, not items given for Temple upkeep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: On all of these I would be strict. When was this said? About things consecrated for the altar. But things consecrated for Temple upkeep do carry מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with רבי יוסי's stricter opinion and a limit on the מעילה rule. This is still part of the source רבא is quoting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי disagrees and would treat a gentile's offerings strictly. The 'no מעילה' rule is limited to קדשי מזבח. Items a gentile gives to בדק הבית are fully subject to מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: To be strict
Things consecrated as offerings for the altar
The Temple upkeep fund
In what case was this said? (a phrase that limits a rule)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
In all of them I see fit to be strict.
In what case was this said?
phrases.notes: This is going back to the 'no מעילה' rule from the start of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: With things consecrated for the altar,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת מוֹעֲלִין בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: but with things consecrated for Temple upkeep, one is liable for misusing them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: בְּכוּלָּן אֲנִי רוֹאֶה לְהַחְמִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that רבא began in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי is strict on all the laws of קדשי גוים. The 'no מעילה' rule applies only to קדשי מזבח, not to בדק הבית.

steps.title: רבא's point: a gentile cannot make a תמורה
steps.stepSummary: רבא points to the one line he needs: the ברייתא says a gentile's offering cannot have a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it teaches: they cannot make a תמורה!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pulls out the key line from the long ברייתא and uses it to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מיהא ('in any case') tells us to ignore the side debates in the ברייתא. Whatever else is argued there, the text plainly says a גוי cannot make a תמורה, so step 11's question seems answered.

keyTerms.meaning: In any case, it teaches (points to the one line that matters)

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:
They cannot make a תמורה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in steps 12–13.
steps.raayaObject: A גוי cannot make a תמורה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The line 'אין עושין תמורה' in the ברייתא

steps.title: רמי בר חמא's real question: who counts, the consecrator or the one atoned?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says the ברייתא only covers a gentile consecrating for himself. His question was about a gentile consecrating an animal that brings atonement to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא could say: I never asked about a גוי who consecrated for a גוי to be atoned. My question is when a גוי consecrated and a ישראל gets the atonement. Do we follow the one who consecrated, or the one who gets atoned?
steps.whatsHappening: The proof is pushed aside. רמי בר חמא explains that his question was about a harder, mixed case that the ברייתא does not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is about a gentile's own offering, where everything is in gentile hands, so it clearly has no תמורה. But if the consecrator is a גוי and the one getting atonement is a ישראל, we need to know whose status decides. If we follow the מקדיש, there is no תמורה. If we follow the מתכפר, there is.

keyTerms.meaning: The person who consecrates the animal
The person who gets atonement from the offering
Do we go after... (whose status decides?)
I am asking / it is a question for me

steps.confusionAlert: The person who consecrates an animal and the person who gets atonement from it can be two different people. This whole question only makes sense once you see that.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question 'do we follow the מקדיש or the מתכפר?' is a key idea that comes back throughout קדשים.

phrases.english: And Rami bar Chama could say:
In a case where a gentile consecrated for a gentile to be atoned,
I was not asking.
When I was asking,
it is where a gentile consecrated and a Jew gets atonement:
do we follow the one who consecrated,
or do we follow the one who gets atoned?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָמֵי בַּר חָמָא, בְּהִקְדִּישׁ גּוֹי לְהִתְכַּפֵּר גּוֹי לָא קָמִיבַּעְיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on רבא's proof by narrowing the question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the use of the ברייתא to answer רמי בר חמא's question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא covers a גוי consecrating for himself, not a mixed case where a ישראל gets the atonement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In a mixed case, whose status decides about תמורה: the מקדיש or the מתכפר?

steps.title: Trying to solve it from רבי אבהו: the one atoned makes the תמורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer from רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן. The מקדיש adds the חומש, but the מתכפר is the one who makes the תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Solve it from רבי אבהו. רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the one who consecrates adds a fifth, and the one who gets atoned makes a תמורה. And one who separates תרומה from his own produce…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רמי בר חמא's question with a rule from רבי יוחנן. The quote keeps going onto the next page.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן splits the laws between two people. The extra fifth on redemption goes with the מקדיש, but the power to make a תמורה goes with the מתכפר. If so, when a ישראל is the מתכפר, it seems he can make a תמורה even though a גוי consecrated the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him solve it (an attempt to answer the question)
The extra fifth added when redeeming one's own consecrated item
One who separates תרומה from his own produce (for someone else's)

phrases.english: Solve it from Rabbi Abahu,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: as Rabbi Abahu said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The one who consecrates adds a fifth,
phrases.notes: This means when the animal is redeemed, for example after it gets a blemish.

phrases.english: and the one who gets atoned makes a תמורה,
and one who separates תרומה from his own produce
